headline: Town boards finalized warrant recommendations ahead of the October 17 Special Town Meeting, debating water line extensions, zoning changes, and major CPA funding requests.
synopsis: October public meetings in Southborough centered on preparations for the October 17 Special Town Meeting, with committees staking out positions on critical warrant articles. The Advisory Committee recommended approving $240,000 from water retained earnings to connect two homes near the contaminated Parkerville Road landfill, while expressing skepticism toward large CPA requests for the municipal golf course irrigation and the Peninsula Trail footbridge. The Community Preservation Committee voted 3-2 to advance the full $217,318 CPA request for the Peninsula Trail bridge despite negative recommendations from both the Advisory Committee and Select Board. In zoning matters, the Zoning Board of Appeals voted to support a proposed two-family dwelling bylaw amendment as drafted, though the Advisory Committee issued an unfavorable recommendation over density and septic concerns. Meanwhile, the Select Board reviewed an opening assessment of town governance structures, and departments advanced initial FY28 budget requests.

top_items.title: Committees divide over Peninsula Trail CPA funding
top_items.why: The Community Preservation Committee voted 3-2 to advance the full $217,318 CPA funding request for the Peninsula Trail footbridge to Special Town Meeting, despite opposition from the Advisory Committee and Select Board.
top_items.body: The proposal for Warrant Article 4 seeks $217,318 in additional CPA funds on top of an existing $211,000 appropriation, bringing the total cost to $428,550 for a 65-foot prefabricated pedestrian bridge along Route 30. The Trails Committee considered a fallback floor amendment that would have eliminated the project contingency to reduce the new ask to $25,000, but dropped the amendment to present the article as written. The Advisory Committee voted 0-7 against the appropriation and the Select Board voted 1-4 against, citing the bridge's estimated cost of roughly $5,000 per linear foot.

top_items.title: Advisory Committee recommends water connections near landfill
top_items.why: The Advisory Committee voted 6-0 to recommend approval of Warrant Article 7, authorizing $240,000 from water retained earnings to connect two homes near the Parkerville Road landfill.
top_items.body: The article funds a water main extension and private service connections for two homes affected by contamination testing near the Parkerville Road landfill. Following clarification from the Select Board chair that the town will cover the service lines from the street into the houses, the Advisory Committee voted unanimously in favor of the warrant article.

top_items.title: Boards split on two-family dwelling zoning amendment
top_items.why: The Zoning Board of Appeals voted to endorse the proposed two-family zoning amendment as drafted, while the Advisory Committee issued an unfavorable recommendation.
top_items.body: Warrant Article 2 proposes easing zoning restrictions on two-family dwellings. The Zoning Board of Appeals reviewed concerns regarding minimum lot requirements across district subsections but chose to endorse the text as written without last-minute edits. In contrast, the Advisory Committee split and issued an unfavorable recommendation, citing concerns about flipping properties without a two-year ownership requirement, lot size impacts in Residential B districts, reliance on percolation tests for septic capacity, and the limited legal protections of special permits.

top_items.title: Advisory and golf officials clash on irrigation funding
top_items.why: The Advisory Committee recommended against spending additional CPA money on Southborough Golf Club irrigation, while the Golf Committee resolved to present the article as written.
top_items.body: The replacement project carries a total cost of $1,087,296, funded by $553,750 approved in 2024, $100,000 from the Golf Revolving Fund, and an additional $433,546 requested in CPA funds at Town Meeting. The Advisory Committee strongly opposed shifting capital costs to taxpayers through CPA funds when the course was intended to be self-funding, pointing to an alternative proposal to borrow $533,000 funded by a $1.50 per-round player surcharge. The Golf Committee authorized $500 for promotional flyers and agreed to keep the article intact on the warrant.

top_items.title: Advisory Committee clarifies stormwater enterprise fund article
top_items.why: The Advisory Committee updated its warrant report to clarify that Article 5 creates an accounting structure but does not levy any stormwater fees.
top_items.body: Article 5 seeks to establish a stormwater enterprise fund as an accounting framework for future stormwater management costs and revenues. The Advisory Committee emphasized in its report that establishing the fund does not implement any user fees, which would require separate Town Meeting approval in the future. The primary purpose discussed was to provide a mechanism to eventually allocate stormwater management costs based on impervious surfaces across all properties, including tax-exempt parcels.

top_items.title: Consultant presents initial municipal governance study
top_items.why: Consultant Bill Keegan delivered an overview of Southborough's governance model and executive authority to the Select Board.
top_items.body: Bill Keegan of Capital Strategic Strategies presented initial findings of a municipal governance structure study. The review evaluated Southborough's organizational model, town manager statutory authority, and committee structures in comparison with peer municipalities across Massachusetts as part of an effort to modernize municipal operations.

top_items.title: Advisory backs appointed Town Clerk with contract protections
top_items.why: The Advisory Committee supported transitioning the Town Clerk from elected to appointed, while recommending contractual termination-for-cause protections.
top_items.body: The Advisory Committee drafted its recommendation in favor of Article 1 to make the Town Clerk an appointed role, noting the increasingly technical nature of the position and municipal trends across Massachusetts. To address resident concerns over losing direct ballot-box accountability, the committee recommended that future employment contracts include explicit termination-for-cause clauses.
